name: Dathí
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dathí was the last pagan king of Ireland. He was a nephew of Niall of the Nine Hostages, and he ruled the province of Connacht for 23 years. When Niall died, Dathí took the kingship at Tara, the great ceremonial seat of the high kings. Tradition places his grave at Cruachan, the provincial capital of Connacht, beneath a standing stone. That stone, say the stories, long predates the reign it is said to mark. Dathí is often dated to the fifth century C.E. There is scholarly doubt about his crown. The more likely truth is that Dathí was never a king. He was a successful warrior who raided the Continent across the sea. Later annalists, eager to praise a patron, raised this warrior to the rank of king and wrote him into the royal line at Tara.
objective: The legend of Dathí, the final pagan king of Ireland, and the standing stone that tradition sets on his grave at Cruachan.
key_results: Dathí was the nephew of Niall of the Nine Hostages.
He ruled Connacht for 23 years before taking the Tara kingship.
Legend places his grave at Cruachan beneath a standing stone.
Historians argue a raider, not a king, was later promoted by annalists.
